title: India orders Pepsi, Red Bull, Monster and others to drop 'energy drink' label despite industry protests
summary: India's food regulator has ordered major beverage makers, including Pepsi, Red Bull and Monster, to stop using the 'energy drink' label on certain products. The directive aims to curb potentially misleading health and performance claims, prompting industry protests and calls for clarification. Companies are expected to amend packaging or seek remedies as regulators push for clearer, standardised labelling to protect consumers.
content:
India's regulator has ordered major beverage makers, including Pepsi, Red Bull and Monster, to stop labelling certain products as 'energy drinks', saying the claims may be misleading and do not meet regulatory definitions.

The move affects multinational and domestic brands whose cans and marketing materials describe their sodas or specialty beverages as energy drinks. Regulators have asked companies to amend packaging and promotional copy to remove the phrase and to ensure product claims align with food safety and labelling rules.

Authorities cited concerns about overstated health and performance claims and said labelling must not mislead consumers. Industry stakeholders counter that consumer demand and established product categories justify the terminology, and some companies have pushed back while seeking clarification from regulators.

The announcement comes amid broader regulatory scrutiny in India’s food and beverage sector, which has included enforcement actions such as licence suspensions and penalties for other violations. Officials say standardising labelling will improve transparency for shoppers and protect public health.

Companies affected are expected either to comply with the directive or to pursue legal or administrative remedies; the timeline for compliance and the precise wording required will be set by the regulator. The decision could have commercial implications for marketing, packaging costs and product positioning in one of the world's largest beverage markets.

Observers say the episode highlights the tension between industry marketing practices and consumer protection rules and underscores how Indian regulators are increasingly active in policing claims on food and drink labels.
